question_text: A personnel file contains alphanumeric codes associated with employees: A-101, B-202, A-102, C-301. How should these be filed?

hint_ladder.title: Hint 1
hint_ladder.text: Think about how you'd file a mix of letters and numbers in a cabinet. What comes first—the letter or the number?

hint_ladder.title: Hint 2
hint_ladder.text: The golden rule for alphanumeric filing: sort by the letter part first (alphabetically), then by the number part (numerically). It's like sorting names by last name, then first name.

hint_ladder.title: Hint 3
hint_ladder.text: Look at the letter parts: A, B, C. Arrange them in alphabetical order first. That gives you A, A, B, C. Now, within the two A's, compare the numbers: 101 and 102. Which is smaller?

hint_ladder.title: Hint 4
hint_ladder.text: So the sequence is: all A's first (with 101 before 102), then B-202, then C-301. That's A-101, A-102, B-202, C-301.

A.text: Correct. This follows the standard rule: sort by letter alphabetically (A, A, B, C), then by number ascending (101, 102, 202, 301). You've got it right.

B.text: This one jumps to B-202 before finishing all the A's. It's a common slip—you might have seen B-202 and placed it next without checking if there were more A's. Remember: all items starting with A must come before any starting with B.

C.text: This puts A-102 before A-101. It's easy to mix up the numbers when you're in a hurry, but 101 is smaller than 102. Think of it like page numbers: page 101 comes before page 102.

D.text: This is completely reversed—starting with C and ending with A. You might have accidentally read the list backwards or thought 'last in, first out.' But filing always goes from A to Z, not Z to A.

deconstruct_text: Let's walk through this like you're actually filing papers. You have four codes: A-101, B-202, A-102, C-301. The first thing you do is ignore the numbers for a moment and look only at the letters. Sort those letters alphabetically: A, A, B, C. That tells you the A's come first, then B, then C. Now, within the A's, you have two codes: A-101 and A-102. Sort those by the number part, smallest to largest. Since 101 is less than 102, A-101 comes before A-102. So your final order is: A-101, A-102, B-202, C-301. Here's a mental trick to remember: think of it like sorting names in a phonebook. You'd sort by last name (the letter) first, and if two people share the same last name, you sort by first name (the number). Same idea here.
next_time_rule: For alphanumeric codes, always file by the letter first (alphabetically), then by the number (numerically). It's like sorting names: last name first, then first name.
